title: MVAC · 28-day schedule
context_label: Urothelial cancer · treatment intent must be specified
indication_text: Neoadjuvant or adjuvant muscle-invasive transitional-cell carcinoma, or locally advanced/metastatic urothelial transitional-cell carcinoma; select the specific treatment intent.
purpose: Treat urothelial cancer before surgery, after surgery, or in advanced disease according to the prescribed indication.
schedule_summary: Methotrexate is given on days 1, 15 and 22; vinblastine on days 2, 15 and 22; doxorubicin and cisplatin on day 2. The cycle repeats every 28 days. NCCP specifies three cycles before surgery, four after surgery, or up to six in metastatic disease; your team records which applies.
administration_text: Treatment is given intravenously. Methotrexate and vinblastine are short administrations; where used, doxorubicin is given through carefully checked access. Cisplatin requires prescribed hydration and a longer visit. The team confirms exact administration and observation times.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests before each cycle; blood count and kidney tests before days 15 and 22. Review infection, mouth, bowel, hearing, nerves, cardiac symptoms and cumulative doxorubicin exposure.
safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital instructions. This information supports a discussion; it does not authorise treatment.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999.

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Methotrexate interferes with folate-dependent reactions that cells need to make DNA. This can slow cancer-cell division, while also affecting blood-cell production and the lining of the mouth and bowel.
agents.watch: Tell the pharmacist about all painkillers, antibiotics, supplements and other medicines because interactions can increase methotrexate toxicity. Report new cough or breathlessness, mouth ulcers, unusual bleeding, jaundice, reduced urine or severe rash promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Mouth ulcers, nausea, diarrhoea and liver-test changes
Kidney injury or slower drug clearance with kidney impairment, dehydration, interacting medicines or fluid collections
Uncommon serious lung inflammation, severe skin reactions and liver injury; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Vinblastine
agents.explanation: Vinblastine prevents cells from separating normally when they divide. It can also affect blood cells, nerves and bowel movement.
agents.watch: Report constipation, abdominal swelling, numbness or pain around the drip.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding
Constipation, sometimes severe bowel blockage or paralysis
Numbness, tingling or weakness from nerve injury
Mouth soreness, nausea and hair loss
Tissue injury if drug leaks outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA and interferes with repair
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care.
agents.watch: Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness and hair loss
Heart muscle damage, sometimes delayed or permanent; risk depends on lifetime exposure and other factors
Tissue injury if drug leaks outside the vein
Temporary red urine after the dose; report painful or persistent red urine
Rare later blood cancer; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Nausea and vomiting, sometimes severe
Kidney injury and low magnesium or other electrolyte changes
Hearing loss or ringing in the ears, which may be lasting
Numbness or tingling from nerve damage, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding
Allergic reactions; possible fertility harm

anatomy: Report new cough or breathlessness urgently.
Report painful ulcers or difficulty drinking.
Chest pain, palpitations, swelling or breathlessness needs urgent advice.
Report constipation early; severe pain, swelling or vomiting needs urgent help.
Report reduced urine, ringing ears or hearing changes; tests guide dosing.
Fever, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning or swelling around the drip.
Report numbness, tingling, weakness or balance changes before the next dose.

cells: Confirm each treatment day, blood-test appointments, support medicines and any growth-factor or folinic-acid prescription.

Treatment is given intravenously. Methotrexate and vinblastine are short administrations; where used, doxorubicin is given through carefully checked access. Cisplatin requires prescribed hydration and a longer visit. The team confirms exact administration and observation times.

Use one written anti-sickness plan, including medicines before treatment, tablets for home and rescue treatment. Your team reconciles steroids, interactions and any stomach-protection medicine from your local prescription. Cisplatin needs prescribed intravenous fluids and electrolyte monitoring/replacement. Follow your own fluid advice; tell the team about heart failure or fluid restriction. Review kidney function, hearing, nerves and other medicines before treatment. Methotrexate interacts with several medicines, including some antibiotics, anti-inflammatory painkillers and proton-pump inhibitors. Do not start, stop or combine medicines without oncology/pharmacy advice. The aprepitant–vinblastine interaction also requires pharmacy reconciliation.
Review lasting effects, support needs and any line/pump removal.

evidence.title: SWOG 8710 · neoadjuvant evidence
evidence.summary: SWOG 8710 compared three cycles of MVAC followed by bladder-removal surgery with surgery alone. Median overall survival was 77 versus 46 months; the two-sided survival comparison had P=0.06. No residual cancer at surgery was found in 38% versus 15%.
evidence.intro: SWOG 8710 compared three cycles of MVAC followed by bladder-removal surgery with surgery alone. Median overall survival was 77 versus 46 months; the two-sided survival comparison had P=0.06. No residual cancer at surgery was found in 38% versus 15%.
evidence.caveat: The survival comparison did not meet the conventional two-sided 0.05 threshold. These results concern neoadjuvant treatment followed by surgery and must not be presented as an adjuvant or metastatic benefit estimate.
evidence.interpretation: The survival comparison did not meet the conventional two-sided 0.05 threshold. These results concern neoadjuvant treatment followed by surgery and must not be presented as an adjuvant or metastatic benefit estimate.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
